from pypdf import PdfReader
from pathlib import Path
r=PdfReader('manuscript.pdf')
p=Path('tmp/pdfs')
p.mkdir(parents=True,exist_ok=True)
print('Pages:',len(r.pages))
parts=[]
for i,page in enumerate(r.pages,1):
    parts.append(f'\\n\\n===== PAGE {i} =====\\n\\n'+page.extract_text())
(p/'manuscript.txt').write_text(''.join(parts))
print(''.join(parts)[:30000])
PY"

/bin/bash -c "python3 - <<'PY'
from pathlib import Path
text=Path('tmp/pdfs/manuscript.txt').read_text()
print(text[text.index('===== PAGE 8 ====='):])
PY"

strengths: Addresses a useful federated-learning problem: selecting specialized models for unseen clients using unlabeled inputs, without local fine-tuning.

The combination of shared routing, pretrained embeddings, sparse expert transmission, and anchor-client supervision is coherent. The equations and Algorithm 1 explain the main training and inference procedures.

Some reported gains are meaningful even against the frozen common expert: 95.7% versus 93% on CIFAR10 in Table 1, and 83.27% versus 73.73% on CIFAR100 with pretrained expert initialization in Table 2.

The ablations examine common-expert quality, expert initialization, anchor frequency, and label heterogeneity. Reporting routing collapse and sensitivity to anchor sampling provides useful information about the method’s operating conditions.
weaknesses: The headline baseline comparison overstates the demonstrated advantage. Table 1 reports a frozen common expert achieving 93% on CIFAR10, so describing approximately 58% as the second-best performance overlooks an available stronger baseline; the improvement over the frozen model is 2.7 percentage points. FedAvg’s deterioration from the 93% initialization to 58.4% also requires diagnosis and evidence of appropriate baseline tuning.

The generalization evidence is narrow: two CIFAR datasets, five CIFAR10 test clients, and ten CIFAR100 test clients. The main experiments explicitly construct anchors with disjoint, collectively exhaustive label subsets and allocate half of each round’s participation to anchors, although they represent only 5–10% of clients. The additional heterogeneity experiment is useful, but does not establish robustness when representative anchors are difficult to identify, unavailable, or poorly matched to incoming clients.

The communication-saving mechanism is plausible, but broader efficiency claims lack measurements of transmitted bytes, runtime, memory, and total computation. Fed-ZERO maintains 5 or 10 experts while the communication-matched FedMix baseline has 2, leaving capacity and routing effects insufficiently separated. Inference also requires the common-model forward pass before the selected expert, and clients store the common model plus downloaded experts.

Reproducibility is insufficiently specified. Important missing details include the common expert’s pretraining procedure and data provenance, the executable client-partition and anchor-selection procedures, gate architecture and embedding choices, and validation/checkpoint-selection protocol. Independent-run counts and the meaning of shaded plot regions are not explained, and no implementation or checkpoint reference is provided.

The routing claims exceed the presented evidence. Table 5 claims 100% routing accuracy, while Appendix C and Table 4 report 5.5% and 27.1% errors without clearly defining routing correctness or distinguishing it from classification correctness. These results do not establish the claimed near-perfect expert selection.

Originality and state-of-the-art positioning need stronger treatment of clustered and mixture-based personalized federated learning, including approaches such as IFCA and FedEM. The manuscript should distinguish the contribution of transferable routing and anchor supervision from existing expert-specialization mechanisms and provide compatible stronger comparisons.

The privacy assurance is too broad. Keeping raw examples local does not establish protection against information leakage through model updates or expert-selection messages. The information required to select label-diverse anchors also needs clarification. A precise threat model or a narrower statement of the privacy properties is necessary.
